conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you today. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been really nauseous, throwing up, and my stomach hurts. It’s been going on for a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You have type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic pancreatitis. Did you take your insulin recently?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No… I ran out four days ago and couldn’t get more. I know I should’ve, but I just didn’t.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s okay. Your blood sugar was very high when you came in—744. That can definitely cause nausea and pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh wow… that’s really high. Is that why I feel so bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We gave you some insulin through an IV to bring it down. Your glucose dropped to 296, which is better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I also have this cough. I went to urgent care a few days ago. They gave me steroids and antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You mentioned prednisone and an antibiotic, but you don’t know which one?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right. I was supposed to take two steroid pills a day. I don’t remember the other one.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a chest X-ray, and your lungs look clear. No pneumonia. Your symptoms sound more like an asthma flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. Should I keep taking the meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We recommend stopping the steroids and antibiotics. You’re on your regular inhalers, which should help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I’ll stop them. Thanks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs show your sodium was low—126—but that’s partly because your blood sugar was so high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that dangerous?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can be, but now that your sugar is coming down, your sodium is correcting on its own. It’s already up to 135.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to start your tube feeds again. You’ve been on them before, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I have a GJ tube. But sometimes they make me feel bloated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor that. If you feel bloated, we can try Maalox. It might help with indigestion.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The tube feeding has started. We’ll go slow and check how you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll let you know if I feel sick.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your nausea and pain have improved. You haven’t vomited since yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I feel a lot better. My stomach’s not as upset.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re keeping an eye on your blood sugar. You had a low this morning—around 60—so we adjusted your insulin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I felt shaky. Is that from the low sugar?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, shakiness, sweating, and dizziness are common with hypoglycemia. We lowered your insulin dose to prevent that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I don’t want to feel like that again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been doing well on the tube feeds, but your blood sugar spiked over 500 after the last one.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh no. Should I stop the feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. But we’re discussing whether to stop them long-term. You’ve been eating well by mouth, which is great.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I have been eating. Maybe I don’t need the tube anymore?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a possibility. We’ll talk more with your primary doctor. If we stop the feeds, your insulin will need adjusting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been on a regular diabetic diet for two days and doing well. No vomiting or severe pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel pretty good. Just a little bloating after the tube feeds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We gave you Maalox for that, and it helped. We also gave IV Zofran and acetaminophen when you felt worse yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, that made me feel better fast.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your HbA1c came back at 11.8%, which shows your sugars have been high over the past few months.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know… I’ve been struggling to keep up with my insulin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re adjusting your insulin regimen. You’ll go home with less insulin on the sliding scale.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I still take Humalog or Regular insulin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue insulin lispro—Humalog. It works faster and is better for mealtime control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I can do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to do when I get home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep taking your insulin as prescribed. Use Maalox if you feel bloated. Stop the steroids and antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the tube feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re not stopping them today, but discuss it with your doctor tomorrow. Your insulin may need lowering if you do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll follow up tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get a printed list of your meds. Review it with your doctor. Call if your sugars are too high or low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for helping me feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before discharge. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I walked to the bathroom and back without any issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Your blood sugar is 117, and you’re not in pain. You’re cleared to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take it easy, and keep up with your care. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve learned my lesson about running out of insulin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. Staying on track will help prevent this from happening again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make sure to refill it on time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. Someone will bring your discharge papers shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll wait for them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also checked your iron levels. They’re low, so keep taking your supplements as prescribed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been forgetting sometimes, but I’ll try to be more consistent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Every bit helps. Small changes can make a big difference over time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do my best.
